## Requirements: Repository-wide Test Runtime resource isolation

**Priority P1. Owner:** Test infrastructure / common runtime composition, Agent/Server/CLI, E2E/Acceptance, Gates. Approved scope from user: review all production-path references used by tests, replace unsafe references, prevent recurrence. Read-only source audit baseline [main@67825f7](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/commit/67825f7a3b121c6653c55dac4149dff8f67eead7). No production mutation or live reproduction performed here.

### Background / dedupe
User observed `Attach: nession-test-flood-928652020-25`. Existing open [#4596](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/4596) records 105 actual leftover flood sessions on /tmp/nession-501/tmux.sock, Nov 24 local host test loops, and owns the immediate real-tmux test-binary fallback/misspelling guard. Keep #4596 independent; this Requirement owns the broader cross-resource policy, E2E destructive-path boundary, all consumers and lifecycle proof. #575/#582/#2520 are historical tmux ownership/reclamation/shared-run contracts; #3155 runtime-dir and #4592 upgrade state continuity remain their own product invariants. Do not reopen or duplicate their existing proof; link #4596 as a scoped implementation dependency where appropriate. This requirement is not a claim that every listed risk already corrupted production.

Synthetic production-like canary only; never reproduce against real user sockets. |

Inject root into manager/context, consistent read/write; replace tests that resolve real home (claude_binding.rs:111+). |

Audit PID/readiness/locks and subprocess stop/status/restart, inject explicit run runtime path. CLI cli_contract.rs:9-13 already sets both. |

Cargo config only rustc-wrapper; wrapper guidance even suggests bare cargo test. Expand existing Gate with negative and valid fixtures plus executable canary proof. |

### Remaining exhaustive audit (mandatory delivery, not claims of confirmed writes)
Enumerate all tracked Rust unit/integration/doc/bench/example/fixture tests, test helpers and their transitive constructors, test binaries and CLI child invocations, shell scripts/gates, JS/TS selftests/web Vitest/Playwright, E2E and Acceptance Cases, native macOS/Linux sandbox/cgroup/mount helpers, container/compose/K8s test lanes and workflows. Produce machine-readable inventory: source + line, resource kind, resolved target, read/write/exec/delete effect, owner, disposition, evidence and replacement. Cover home/runtime/legacy PID migration, config/credentials/identity/token, logs, Session history, metadata, env store/bindings, Claude/Codex MCP/trust/hooks/transcripts, SQLite sidecars, image build/blob/CAS/cache/EROFS, workspace/project roots, overlay mounts/leases/cgroups, install/update/archive/service manager, Git config/worktrees/SSH agents, shell history/rc, browser profiles/artifacts, fixed sockets/ports/HTTP APIs, GitHub/OCI/provider/remote Store credentials and network. Read-only OS probes (/proc, /sys, system executables), serialized example strings, in-sandbox virtual paths such as /tmp, explicit TempDir fixtures and intentionally shared build caches with safe concurrency are not automatically defects: classify and justify. Native delegated cgroup root is approved only with a unique owned child subtree and actual capability proof; never run destructive tests on host production paths. No global replace of path strings or production defaults. Initial spot review found EROFS compose temp root, Claude trust temp fixtures, server full_stack temp DB, CLI cli_contract private home/runtime, and loopback :0 Agent helpers; retain these safe patterns. Audit remaining paths before claiming completeness.

### Design decision: one Test Runtime resource owner
- Introduce/reuse a single canonical TestRuntime/TestContext owner for run identity, private root, durable home, runtime dir, OS home, XDG config/cache/data/state, tool configs, tmux socket, DB/cache/workspace/fixture roots, endpoint allocation and child env; choose implementation language/adapters at existing Rust common + JS/shell harness boundaries. Avoid another production path resolver. Production defaults remain unchanged; tests inject explicit roots and typed resource contexts. Prefer ownership held by TempDir/RAII rather than leaked dirs, PID+counter or global env. Process-scoped context installed before first access; nested runs can reuse only verified parent capability, never arbitrary inherited ENV. Bare Cargo may auto-init or fail closed (#4596 chooses fail closed for tmux); no bypass based solely on executable filename or cfg(test) as integration deps/subprocess production binaries also run in tests.
- Suggested layout: short mkdtemp run root with manifest (run_id, owner PID/start identity, uid, canonical root, resource inventory, lifecycle state); home/, runtime/, user-home/, tool-config/, workspace/, cache/, db/, logs/, artifact/, sockets/ (short socket path within Unix limit). Exclusive create, no symlink escape, ownership validation before any destructive operation; PID alone/name prefix/socket self-report not proof. Separate test build/cache sharing from mutable runtime state. All test entrypoints consume owner; explicit isolated child env allowlist and test-only auth; loopback owned endpoints, hermetic default with remote egress/credentials only for declared dedicated test lane. Do not blanket remove required compiler PATH or read-only OS dependencies.
- Replace default/ambient references via constructor injection (SessionMetadataStore::with_root, binding roots, explicit config/store/paths), isolated subprocess env, per-run manifests and test service adapters. No `kill-server` / rm -rf / service uninstall on live/unknown resources; exact target identity + owner proof; teardown order: stop admission, settle/abort jobs, stop child processes, release mounts/cgroup/leases, kill owned tmux, verify, remove owned root. Preserve cleanup-failed records for reaper; not delete socket directory if kill/refusal uncertain. Legacy leak cleanup is explicit dry-run and per-session evidence; user prefix not authority; never auto-delete real Sessions.
- Extend existing `scripts/check-test-isolation.sh`/Gate and detector self-tests; use source inventory and end-to-end synthetic sentinels as complementary proof, not regex-only claims. Update scoped instructions, test commands and canonical docs; no skipped/serialized suites to hide regressions.

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 Every supported test entry (bare cargo test/IDE/direct binary, wrapper, cargo llvm-cov, gate, E2E/Acceptance, subprocess CLI) either obtains a verified private resource context before side effects or fails closed with actionable diagnostics; unset, blank, misspelled, inherited production-like, symlink and foreign-run paths are rejected before touching canaries.
- [x] SC-02 All real-tmux and Agent tests use owned socket, metadata, binding, shell/workspace and env roots; a synthetic live Agent on a separate socket keeps identical server PID/session/pane identity and configuration/state hashes while test creates, attaches, mutates and cleans its own resources. Include #4596 regression, not a second implementation.
- [x] SC-03 All Server/Agent/CLI tests resolve durable home, OS runtime, DB/WAL, identity/token/config/logs, image/cache and service/install roots within owned test context or explicit read-only fixture. Parallel update/path tests and child start/stop/restart cannot touch synthetic host sentinel files, PID state or unrelated processes; no global env leakage.
- [x] SC-04 E2E/Acceptance runner allocates unique roots/ports, binds to owned loopback listeners and publishes run manifest. Two independent runs can coexist, stop/restart one without affecting the other; inherited/forged production-looking home/socket, symlink and foreign owner are rejected before rm/kill, and browser session lifecycle regression passes.
- [x] SC-05 Default test children use private HOME/XDG/tool-specific config and sanitized environment; synthetic host credentials, Git/SSH config, Claude/Codex transcript/trust, tokens/proxies and arbitrary inherited endpoint cannot be read or forwarded by default. Mock HTTP/WS/registry endpoints prove no unexpected dial; explicit authenticated integration uses separate approved test namespace and is not exercised against production.
- [x] SC-06 Normal completion, panic/assert, failed partial startup, timeout, SIGTERM and SIGKILL of a disposable run leave no live owned resources after bounded teardown/reaper; reaper proves run ownership, never kills live/foreign or deletes unverified dirs, and preserves auditable failure evidence. Legacy mixed-socket diagnostics dry-run and require explicit scoped authorization, never name-prefix-only deletion.
- [x] SC-07 Existing test-isolation Gate rejects negative fixtures for direct/indirect default paths, inherited prod socket/root, fixed active endpoint, global env races, unsafe cleanup, shell/JS/E2E entry bypass; accepts path-string serialization, read-only fixtures, explicit temp roots and intentional same-run sharing. Inventory covers every crate and test entry, every path reference classified and no unresolved actionable item remains at closure.

### Proof routing
SC-01/03/05/07: SCN-01 deterministic contract, exact PR SHA source + existing rust-test, detector and E2E CI receipts with adversarial fixtures. SC-02/04/06: SCN-03 runtime lifecycle, exact merged staging SHA targeted runtime Cases with real local Server/Agent/tmux/PTY/process and synthetic sentinel home/socket, approved existing CI runtime harness; SC-06 native Linux/macOS resources only when native runner capability and isolated delegated subtree available, otherwise Pending. All positive/negative tests use disposable fixtures; no production secrets/services. Use exact SHA/Run/Attempt, before/after hashes, PID/pane identity, observed endpoint logs, owner manifests and teardown evidence. Verification tier integration, no generic Full Regression closure dependency. E2E session-lifecycle covers regression only, not a substitute for runtime isolation proof.

### Knowledge Impact
- Decision: Update
- Related knowledge: docs/architecture/agent-tmux-test-isolation.md, docs/architecture/session-tmux-sdk-ownership.md, test-isolation Gate, existing runtime harness documentation.
- Reason: establish one cross-resource isolation/lifecycle contract, update existing tmux test notes to describe all supported entrypoints and failure behavior.
- Owner and timing: developer during implementation; Reviewer checks exact source and knowledge links prior to acceptance.
- Evidence: inventory, canonical docs diff and Gate/Case receipts at exact SHA.
